### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `822c41ead92de9f0c79ff952a39840ad91e265c4` — the merge of head `deefadb3a13681d5e31f584317f73a7a92c270e2` into base `f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 822c41ead92de9f0c79ff952a39840ad91e265c4 && git checkout 822c41ead92de9f0c79ff952a39840ad91e265c4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba deefadb3a13681d5e31f584317f73a7a92c270e2 && git checkout -B drift-repro f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba && git merge --no-ff deefadb3a13681d5e31f584317f73a7a92c270e2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `deefadb3a13681d5e31f584317f73a7a92c270e2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.data-table-staged-edit-retired.ts + ui/packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/complex/dataTableBindDiagnostic.ts, ui/packages/components/src/context/gridCellSelection.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/objectGridRowVersion.ts, ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/objectGridTranslations.ts, ui/packages/types/src/data-display.ts, ui/packages/types/src/objectql.ts, ui/packages/types/src/zod/data-display.zod.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceListPage.tsx
Security-touching: no

PR #37437, card #35827, ruling 7178367040 (option A). Inputs read: the card body and its 12 comments, PR #37314's body (it opened protocol step 19), the PR body and its 2 comments, the net diff of 69 files against `origin/main` (merge base `df0894a664`), the 74 check-runs on the head, and both attempts of run 45789943743. The template prints no security line on this face; the one above is written because the dispatch asked for it, and nothing on this PR's landing path reads it.

### ① Derived judgments

What the diff takes away, each read in the head tree:

- `ObjectGridComponentProps.cellSelection`: `boolean` becomes `true` (`ObjectGrid.tsx:452`). Right. At runtime `hostCellSelection = cellSelectionProp === true || inlineEditable` (`:1335`), so an editable grid is always select-first and `false` can no longer keep the staged arm.
- `ObjectGridComponentProps.onBatchSave`: declaration deleted, destructuring deleted, `defaultBatchSave` and `saveRowsClaimed` deleted, and the `onBatchSave ?? defaultBatchSave` wire on the built `data-table` node deleted. Right. `ObjectGridComponentProps` has no index signature, so an explicit JSX attribute is an excess-property error.
- `DataTableSchema.onBatchSave`: the TS face is `?: never` (`data-display.ts:1798`) and the zod mirror moves from `'runtime-slot'` to `'retired'` (`data-display.zod.ts:544`). Right. The parse refused the key by name before and still does; only the disposition and its message changed. Pinned by `RetiredIsNever` and the 60/23 ledger counts in `handler-keys-json-refusal-6124.test.ts`.
- `DataTableSchema.singleClickEdit`: deleted from the interface. It never had a zod arm (it was a `RuntimeOnlyDeclared` key). Right as a removal: `BaseSchema` carries no index signature, so a fresh literal that sets it fails `tsc`. It is a deletion, not this package's `?: never` tombstone; see N1.
- `data-table` behaviour: `editable = editableProp && selectFirst && typeof schema.onRowSave === 'function'` (`data-table.tsx:1668-1669`). The pending-changes bar, Save All, Cancel All, the row save and cancel buttons, the edit-only column header, click-to-edit, the amber tints, `saveRow`, `saveBatch`, `erroredRows` and the non-select-first focus-return branch are gone. Right. Each removed branch was reachable only with `selectFirst` false or `autosaves` false, and `editable` is now false in both.
- Exports removed: `BatchSaveOutcome` (`objectGridRowVersion.ts`, an internal module) and five fallback copy rows in `TABLE_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS`. Right. One export is added: `describeUnsavableEditable` with `DATA_TABLE_EDITABLE_DIAGNOSTIC_PREFIX`.
- Record verdicts: the `updateOnMount` argument is dropped from the one `useRecordCrudVerdicts` call. Right. It was true only when `inlineEditable && !hostCellSelection`, which cannot hold any more.
- Declarations: the PR body and the changeset both carry line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. The changeset has the BREAKING banner, a five-row FROM/TO table, the one-line fix and the marker `adr-0087: registered data-table-staged-edit-retired`. Each removed item above has its FROM/TO row. `narrowed` is the ruled kind (term 4) and holds on content: a `data-table` key leaves the interface, and an authored `editable: true` with no save path is now refused where it used to stage.

The −2787 lines are dead at the head. Greps of the whole head tree, covering docs, skills, examples and tests:

- `defaultBatchSave`, `BatchSaveOutcome`, `saveRowsClaimed`, `saveBatch`, `cancelAllChanges`, `cancelRowChanges`, `erroredRows`, `pendingCellFocusRef`, `table-save-refusal`: zero code references. One stale comment survives (N5).
- `onBatchSave`: only the tombstone, the zod refusal, the comments that explain the retirement, the pins, the docs' upgrade lines and the changesets.
- `cellSelection={false}`, `cellSelection: false`, `onBatchSave=`: zero in `ui/**`, `examples/**`, `packages/**` and `skills/**`, outside prose that names the retirement.
- `skills/**` and `examples/**`: zero hits for `onBatchSave`, `cellSelection`, Save All, `saveAll`. The PR's `Skills-docs: none` holds.
- No host other than `ObjectGrid` builds an editable `data-table` or supplies `onRowSave`. `GridCellSelectionProvider` is mounted in one place, `ObjectGrid.tsx:5325`. So no in-tree surface falls into the new read-only arm.
- `git merge-tree` of the head onto `origin/main` at `54ea3c8c38` is clean. The 8 commits `main` gained since the PR's last merge add no use of any retired name.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/components`, `@object-ui/plugin-grid`, `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@objectstack/spec` matches AGENTS.md: a `narrowed` kind takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves, and a breaking change keeps its banner at that level. `@objectstack/spec: minor` goes with the entry file, as in #37314. `@object-ui/data-objectstack` and `@object-ui/plugin-list` change comments only and rightly carry no bump. `Check Changeset` and its ADR-0087 step are green on the head.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — correct. Nothing is widened; `describeUnsavableEditable` is an added export of a diagnostics module, not an accept-set.

### ③ Boundary flags

- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff holds no query, id materialisation or join.
- `open_questions` in the os-dev report: empty.
- **Approval for the `packages/spec` entry: none is recorded.** The claim 7181103894 fences out `packages/spec/**`. Fence amendment 1 (7181311810) admits the entry file, but it is the seat's own comment and quotes no maintainer. The PR body and the os-dev report say the maintainer approved it by name; no comment on the card or the PR quotes that approval, and the o5-U thread is outside this review's inputs. Ruling term 4 does order an ADR-0087 entry, and such entries live only under `packages/spec`. Escalated: the maintainer lands this PR himself (over 3000 lines), so his merge is the approval; a quoted line on the card would close the record.
- Dogfood battery: the report's `dogfood_battery` opens with `deefadb3`, the 8-hex prefix of the head, not the full 40-hex sha. `BATTERY_SHA_SHAPE` in `label-write.mjs` takes 7 to 40 hex, so the land gate reads it as pinned to this head. Reported: VERDICT command-exit 0, 487 files passed and 3 skipped of 490, 4129 tests passed and 68 skipped of 4197, no failure. Full battery, on the final head, as ruling term 4 asks.
- Test Core (5/10), attempt 1: **unrelated to this diff.**
  - Signature: `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/data-commands.absent-database.integration.test.ts:703:3`, `Hook timed out in 480000ms`. A timeout, not an assertion. The run reported 220 of 221 files passed and 2732 tests passed.
  - It is a known flake: open card #37183, filed 2026-11-25 against merge-queue run 45528039199 of #37155, same shard, same file, same line.
  - Attempt 2 of the same job on the same head is green, and all 74 check-runs on the head are success or skipped.
  - Does a changed path feed the test? Nominally yes: the hook spawns the source CLI 46 times, the CLI imports `@objectstack/spec`, and the diff adds one spec file. That file is a 36-line constant of strings and adds no work to a boot. No path under `packages/cli` is in the diff.
  - So the first of the seat's three facts (import closure disjoint from the diff) does not hold on its letter, and the re-run stands on the known-signature branch instead. The audit comment that branch asks for is not on the PR; the PR body and the report carry the account.
- The three noted-not-filed items:
  - Dead locale keys (`table.saveAll`, `table.cancelAll`, `table.modified`, `table.saveRow`, `table.cancelChanges`; still in the locale packs, no reader): no new card. Dead strings are outside the filing gate. They belong to the v19 line's existing `@object-ui/i18n` retirement of released keys no code reads; a comment on that family's card carries them.
  - `ui/packages/fields/README.md:145-149` and `FieldEditWidget.tsx:216-219`: **needs a card.** The README ships in the package (`files[]`) and still says a grid without `cellSelection` opens the rich-text box over the cell and keeps the text for the grid's save buttons. After this PR that is wrong text that a release fixes in place, which is the filing gate's release-text exception. The card should also check whether the over-the-cell branch behind those lines is now unreachable.
  - `useRecordCrudVerdicts`' `updateOnMount` option (`useRecordCrudVerdicts.ts:521`, no caller, internal hook): no card. Dead code; the acceptance note is its record.
  - The report files all three as `class: c`. None is: class c is a metadata trap with a named producer, and these are dead strings, stale prose and dead code.
- `content/docs/releases/v19/index.mdx:273-275` says `protocol-18-range-refused` sits on the protocol-19 step and the other 30 on step 18. With this entry step 19 holds two. The page is release-owned and outside this diff; the release seat should hear of it.
- Security: no hunk moves a permission, sharing, credential or token boundary. Editing only narrows (`editable` now also needs a save path). The surviving save path keeps its rule check, `If-Match` guard and conflict dialog (`defaultRowSave`, `writeRowInPlace`). The dropped `updateOnMount` served only the removed arm. The migrated permission pins (`inlineEditPermissionGate`, `inlineEditFieldWriteGrant-12103`, `maskedColumnSurfaces-10583`) drive the gesture that would open an editor (select, then double-click or Enter) and keep their controls. The report's `security_findings` is `none`.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

The entry file, `19.data-table-staged-edit-retired.ts`:

- Form: a `SemanticMigration` with `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria`, and no `conversionIds`. Correct for a D3 entry with no D2 conversion.
- Step: 19 is right. `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is `19.0.0` at the head, `registry.ts.template` declares `step19` with a generated `semantic:19` block, and #37314 records that a v19-line retirement filed under step 18 is not shown to an 18-to-19 upgrader. The template is rightly untouched: entries are added as files, and the step's rationale is one string.
- Surface, replacement and reason agree with the code sentence by sentence: `cellSelection` takes only `true`; a host may still pass `true`; an editable `data-table` without both a cell-selection host and `onRowSave` renders read-only and warns; nothing authorable is rewritten.
- The acceptance text says the type check refuses all the retired spellings. That holds for typed call sites and literals (N1 and N2 name its edge).

The narrowing against the ruling:

- Term 1 (staged arm, `onBatchSave` on both interfaces, `cellSelection={true}` kept, absent means editable is select-first and read-only is click-to-open): implemented as ruled.
- Term 2 (bare-primitive arm): the dev chose loud refusal. It sits at the right door, the renderer, where `editable` is resolved and where the module's sibling diagnostics already speak, on the same channel (`console.warn`, keyed on the message, prefix `[ObjectUI] DataTable editable:`). It holds for no host, for a host without `onRowSave`, and for a host with `onBatchSave` alone, which is the old staged-under-select-first arm and is now read-only with the `onRowSave` line. Pinned in `data-table-autosave-35685.test.tsx:272-311` by three cases: no provider, provider without `onRowSave`, and a read-only control that warns nothing.
- Term 3 (pins): three test files deleted with the behaviour they pinned, the rest migrated to select-first gestures. `keyboardNavigation`'s jsdoc lost its staged sentence.
- Term 4: declarations, entry and battery as above.
- Premise clause: the census (hotcrm `fb0b879`, gallery `782d801`, 0 hits) is the dev's reading. Those repos are outside this review's inputs, so it is not re-measured here.

Ways an author can still write the old mode, and what each meets:

| Spelling | What it meets |
|:--|:--|
| typed host, `cellSelection={false}` on `ObjectGrid` | `tsc` error |
| typed host, `onBatchSave` on `ObjectGrid` | `tsc` excess-property error |
| `onBatchSave` on a `DataTableSchema` value | `tsc` error (`never`) |
| `onBatchSave` in a JSON document | zod refusal by name, as retired |
| editable `data-table` with no host or no `onRowSave` | read-only, one console warning naming what is missing |
| untyped or cast host passing `cellSelection={false}` or `onBatchSave` to `ObjectGrid` | nothing at runtime (N2) |
| `singleClickEdit` on a `data-table` node in a document | parses, inert (N1) |

Nits. None changes correctness or the contract; each is an accepted deviation or a follow-up, and none needs a head move.

- N1 (nit) — `DataTableSchema.singleClickEdit` is deleted, not left as this package's `?: never` tombstone (`objectql.ts:1337` states that convention). A non-literal value, or a document through the mirror's `.passthrough()`, still carries it in silence. It is harmless alone: the key only chose how the staged editor opened, and its companion `editable: true` now warns.
- N2 (nit) — `ObjectGrid` says nothing at runtime to an untyped host that still passes `cellSelection={false}` or `onBatchSave`. The grid turns select-first and writes each cell through `onRowSave` or its own `dataSource.update`, and the batch handler is never called. The ruling names the type error as the door, so this complies. No test pins the narrowed prop type (`cellSelection` is `true | undefined`; `onBatchSave` is not a key of the props), so a later widening would pass every test.
- N3 (nit) — the warning text and the changeset tell the author to mount `GridCellSelection`. That is the context's value type; the component to mount is `GridCellSelectionProvider` (`components/src/index.ts:187`).
- N4 (nit) — the retired refusal for `onBatchSave` uses the generic `handlerKeyRefusal` text: it cites objectui#6124 and points at a toast or action node, not at `onRowSave` or `object-grid`, which is this retirement's FROM/TO.
- N5 (nit) — leftovers in tests: `plugin-form/src/affordanceGrantMap-12082.test.tsx:909` still names `defaultBatchSave` in a comment; two assertions query the removed `data-table-edit-column-header` test id and can only read null (`data-table-autosave-35685.test.tsx:130`, `data-table-select-first-35684.test.tsx:339`); case e of `inlineEditPermissionGate.test.tsx` now compares two shapes that cannot differ.
- N6 (nit) — the card's original Done-when asked for `git grep onBatchSave ui/` to read zero outside the entry and its tests. The head keeps a `never` tombstone and a by-name refusal instead. That is the stricter of the two and follows the re-premise in ruling 7178367040; recorded as an accepted deviation.

- 要你做什么：批准并合并。超过 3000 行（4040 行），需要人合并。契约复核 PASS 在评论 7189751333，Head-sha `deefadb3a13681d5e31f584317f73a7a92c270e2`。
